text: Mac Dathó was an Irish hero, also called Mac Datho or Mes Roeda. He is the hero of the Ulster Cycle tale Scéla mucce Meic Dathó. He was a warrior whose prize hunting hound Ailbe drew the desire of two kings, Conchobar mac Nessa of Ulster and Ailill mac Máta of Connacht. He could refuse neither ruler, so he invited both with their warriors to a feast. There he served an immense roasted pig. The finest champion always received the best part of a feast, so an argument broke out over who would be honored. In the melee the hound Ailbe was killed, which gave Mac Dathó a solution to his problem.
